header:
Date: 2026-06-29T15:00Z UTC | Duration: ~78 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Santos (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (Harborlane Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (Harborlane SRE), Ravi Patel (Harborlane CTO), Dana Park (Security)
summary: Post-incident run-through focusing on a staged "shadow" deployment to validate remediation steps without impacting live traffic. Objectives: validate rollback triggers, confirm KV cache warm-up strategies, measure latency regressions, and obtain customer acceptance criteria for production rollforward. Agreement to run a controlled shadow deploy and replay traffic with a follow-up executive acceptance call.
topics: Incident recap and root cause hypotheses
Shadow deploy plan and safety controls
KV cache warm-up and prefix caching strategy
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): okay we're live. thanks everyone for coming, appreciate the quick turnaround on this. uh today is a run-through, sort of a shadow deploy simulation following the incident last week where we saw long tail latencies during peak bursts. we wanted to validate our mitigations end-to-end, and get explicit acceptance criteria from harborlane.
[00:25] Marta (Harborlane): thanks jordan. quick note, we're recording so we'll share with ops. main ask is we cannot have any customer-visible errors during the test, even 0.01% is a problem for us because of downstream billing.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): got it, and that's why the plan is shadow-only; traffic will be forked, not proxied. we will run the same traffic against the new rollout and measure delta on p50/p95/p99 and error rates, no traffic will be written to prod backends.
[00:58] Ethan (Harborlane SRE): just to be clear, when you say forked, does that include KV cache priming? last time the cold cache contributed a lot of the latency.
[01:12] Priya: yes that was a big learning. for this run we'll do a two-phase warm-up: prefix replay for the top 10k prefixes, then a synthetic warm-up to exercise the long tail. we'll also test the prefix cache TTL changes we proposed.
[01:29] Ravi (CTO): and the commit point here is what? if shadow shows p99 degradation of more than 10% do we roll back? what's the threshold? we need hard limits.
[01:40] Jordan: good question. proposed acceptance criteria in the playbook: p95 increase under 7% and p99 under 12% for baseline synthetic workload; error rate increase under 0.02% absolute. otherwise we consider automatic abort and further tuning.
[01:57] Marta: that 12% p99 seems high. can we pair that with a latency SLA compensation clause? we need mitigation for customers impacted.
[02:08] Jordan: yes we can include a compensation trigger but first let's see the numbers. liam, can we make sure legal is looped for the SLA wording?
[02:17] Liam (CSM): yes i'll loop legal and add a draft addendum, i'll share by end of day.
[02:25] [02:25] Speaker 6 (unknown): um so, i had a quick question about observability hooks — are you pushing the same span ids in the shadow runs so we can cross-correlate?
[02:35] Priya: great catch. yes we will annotate shadow spans with a x-shadow header and preserve trace ids so both systems can be correlated in datadog and jaeger. we'll also snapshot KV cache hit rates and the kv-hit-by-prefix metric.
[02:50] Ethan: last time our audit log ingestion got overloaded, that was a surprising cascade. have you changed the log export rate?
[02:59] Priya: we added a sampling gate on low-importance traces and throttled export to the ingestion pipeline during warmups. full logs for error events will still be recorded but we won't flood the pipeline with debug-level telemetry.
[03:14] Marta: security is watching this closely, dana do you want to comment?
[03:18] Dana (Security): yes. two items: (1) we need to ensure KMS keys used for any crypto are not re-used in a way that violates rotation policies during the test, and (2) audit logs must be immutable and exported to our S3 bucket within the 24-hour window.
[03:35] Priya: understood, priya note: we'll use a separate ephemeral key ring for the shadow environment and confirm export hooks. we'll produce a short assurance doc for dana.
[03:50] [03:50] Jordan: okay moving on to rollback triggers, priya can you walk the automated guardrails?
[03:56] Priya: yes so automated guardrails are: if 5xx rate increases by 0.01 absolute in a 2-minute window OR p99 increases by more than the threshold set (12% default) OR anomalous CPU/GPU utilization > 90% for 60s, system will mark the rollout as failed and we will not promote to canary. the rollback is non-destructive — we'll stop routing and deprovision the rollout worker set. note that for shadow we will simulate this path, not actually deprovision live nodes.
[04:30] Ethan: i need the exact metric names so we can wire alerts. what are the exact metric keys?
[04:35] Priya: metrics: "redwood.request.duration.p50/p95/p99", "redwood.request.errors.5xx", "redwood.kv.cache.hit_rate", "redwood.node.gpu_util_pct". i'll share a metrics mapping doc.
[04:50] Jordan: great. another operational question — last incident had a kv cache corruption edge case when a certain sequence of prefix evictions happened. have you patched that?
[05:02] Priya: yes we patched a race in the eviction path; we've added a compare-and-swap guard. however we want to validate at scale because it's timing-sensitive. the shadow replay will include eviction-heavy traffic.
[05:18] Marta: can you run the eviction scenario with our backpressure profile? we run bursts up to 3x normal every thursday.
[05:27] Priya: absolutely, ethan can you share the thursday burst replay window and we'll fold it into the test.
[05:33] Ethan: i'll share the replay artifact by Friday, includes headers and sticky session patterns.
[05:38] [05:38] Jordan: okay let's talk about the communication plan if we see regressions during the test. recommended: immediate ops channel alert, then 10-mines, 30-mines, and 1-hour updates to the incident channel and to harborlane slack. draft templates will be attached to the runbook.
[05:58] Ravi: one concern: last time the fallback path activated and gave stale responses — we need to prove that fallback does not return stale data beyond X minutes. can we include a freshness check in the shadow validation?
[06:12] Priya: yes we'll add a freshness verifier: sample requests will be labeled "freshness-check" and we'll verify item timestamps. if stale ratio > 0.1% we fail the test.
[06:25] Marta: security question again, does the shadow run touch PII? we need assurance it doesn't write customer PII to any new stores.
[06:33] Priya: no writes to external stores in shadow; reads only, and any sensitive fields will be redacted (simple tokenization) in the shadow path. we'll show the tokenization map.
[06:45] [06:45] Speaker 6 (unknown): small nit, in the playbook you have a human-in-loop step at T+20 minutes for manual abort. can that be reduced? in high-throughput incidents we might want faster human intervention.
[06:59] Jordan: we put human-in-loop to give customers the ability to stop. we can make it T+10 with an option to auto-abort if the metric breach is severe. we'll formalize that.
[07:12] Liam: i'll note that product ops can enable auto-abort threshold toggles if harborlane signs the delegated ops agreement.
[07:22] [07:22] Priya: okay to the schedule: we'll do a dry run in staging tomorrow at 09:00 local, then the shadow deploy in prod-sim Friday at 03:00 UTC, and the full replay on Monday during the agreed window. timeline posted in the runbook.
[07:38] Ethan: question about resource isolation — will the shadow workers share the same GPU pool? last time OOM killed inference processes.
[07:47] Priya: for the shadow run we will spin up an isolated worker pool with soft quotas, separate GPU reservation. it will still use same physical hosts for cost reasons but via cgroups and GPU partitioning we isolate. we'll also simulate OOM by introducing memory pressure in a canary to confirm graceful degradation.
[08:10] Marta: what about billing implications of the shadow run? we need to know cost delta before approval.
[08:17] Jordan: we'll provide a cost estimate — rough order of magnitude expressed as delta per hour plus peak GPU hours. liam will include cost breakout in the next email.
[08:27] [08:27] Dana: onboarding note for logs: we require sha256 hashes for payloads stored in our audit pipeline to guarantee immutability. can the export include a manifest?
[08:36] Priya: yes we can generate a manifest with sha256 and a signed timestamp. we'll push to your S3 ingest endpoint.
[08:44] [08:44] Jordan: okay, quick recap of risks: cache corruption, audit ingestion overload, cold-start tail latency, unexpected fallback staleness. mitigations: eviction fix, log sampling, prefix warm-up, freshness checks. any other risks?
[09:00] Ravi: supply chain concern — model weights changed in the last onboarding, did you validate kernel selection? small changes in quantization params cause different memory patterns.
[09:12] Priya: we validated the kernel selection matrix and pinned quantization seeds for this runtime; we also added a guard that rejects variants with unknown quant seeds at rollout time. we'll include the kernel matrix in the runbook.
[09:30] [09:30] Speaker 6: are we doing a canary after shadow or direct promote?
[09:35] Jordan: canary after shadow. shadow -> canary (0.1% serving) -> ramp if green. canary will be run in a smaller frac with auto-abort.
[09:45] Marta: what does acceptance look like for us? we want an exec sign-off checklist.
[09:50] Jordan: we'll prepare an acceptance doc with explicit metrics: p50/p95/p99 deltas, error delta, freshness rate, cache hit rate target, ingestion queue health, and audit export success. that's the checklist for sign-off.
[10:07] [10:07] Priya: demo note: during the staging dry run we'll capture dashboards and produce a 10-min summary video for execs.
[10:14] Ethan: for the replay artifact, can we include header-level cookies and sticky session sim? our sessions are sticky and that altered behavior previously.
[10:22] Priya: yes include sticky session headers, we have mapping rules to simulate session affinity.
[10:29] Jordan: ok, some housekeeping: who owns what doc? priya runbook, ethan replay artifact, jordan remediation playbook, liam sla/legal, dana security checklist, rita (not here) will be communications.
[10:43] Marta: rita is on vacation this week, liam can you handle exec comms?
[10:48] Liam: yes i'll handle communications and draft the exec brief.
[10:52] [10:52] Jordan: let's walk through a hypothetical timeline in the runbook, live-fire example: T0 start replay, T+5 observe rising p99, T+8 check freshness, T+10 human abort or auto-abort if breach severe. what does harborlane want the escalation ladder to look like?
[11:09] Marta: immediate on-call, then platform lead, then CTO. for external comms we want a single named contact — that would be liam.
[11:20] Jordan: noted. one more technical detail — are there any firewall or VPC egress constraints that will block your ability to receive audit exports?
[11:28] Dana: our bucket only accepts signed requests from known ip cidrs, we'll share the updated allowlist.
[11:33] Priya: we'll test the S3 handshake in staging with the allowlist before the shadow run.
[11:40] [11:40] Ethan: i want to run a resilience script that introduces packet jitter and small delays to see effect on tail. ok to run in prod-sim?
[11:46] Priya: yes in prod-sim that's fine, just capture telemetry. we'll not run it during the production replay window unless explicitly authorized.
[11:56] Jordan: ok 10 minute checkpoint, any blockers outstanding?
[12:01] Ethan: replay artifact pending but on track.
[12:05] Marta: legal review on SLA wording pending until liam's draft.
[12:09] Dana: security checklist will be shared tomorrow.
[12:12] Jordan: good. moving to runbook specifics — i'll highlight the manual rollback steps and the script to verify rollback idempotency.
[12:21] Priya: a nuance — some of the rollback steps require a brief DNS TTL flush; that can take up to 30s for some customers, so we factor that into the time-to-recovery estimate.
[12:36] Ravi: can you provide measured TTR (time-to-recover) from the staging dry run? we'll need that for our on-call escalation matrices.
[12:43] Priya: yes staging dry run will produce TTR numbers. expected TTR target is under 180s median, worst-case under 10 minutes.
[12:55] Jordan: perfect. let's record final decisions and owners.
[13:00] [13:00] Quick recap (verbatim):
- Shadow deploy: forked traffic, no writes, separate ephemeral keys, isolated worker pool.
- Warm-up: prefix replay (10k) + synthetic tail exercise.
- Guardrails: p99/p95 thresholds, 5xx absolute rate, GPU util breach, freshness checks.
- Logs: sampling for debug traces, full error export, signed manifest to S3.
- Acceptance: exec sign-off doc with metrics and stale-check thresholds.
[13:40] Marta: i appreciate the thoroughness. one last asks: can we get a runbook dry-run recording? our execs like a short clip.
[13:52] Jordan: yes we'll capture a 10-min highlight clip from the staging dry run.
[13:58] Liam: scheduling note, i'll propose a slot for the exec acceptance for week of 2026-07-06 and send calendar invites after we confirm results.
[14:06] Jordan: sounds good. any final comments?
[14:12] Dana: please ensure the assurance doc covers key rotation and manifest signing.
[14:18] Ethan: ping me when the replay artifact is uploaded.
[14:22] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the runbook link and the checklist. meeting adjourned.
[14:30] End of recording.

Note: transcript contains natural stutters, occasional speaker attribution errors and periodic timestamps approximate the flow; some segments auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "5xx" might be read as "five x" in parts).
questions: What are the hard thresholds for rollback (p95/p99/error rate)?
Will the shadow run write any PII or require special key handling?
What are the exact metric names to wire alerts?
Who signs off on exec acceptance and what's the timeline?
